title: Cross-Domain Falsification and Runtime Foundations v1 Reconstruction
results: No RF0-RF15 contradiction requires reopening a prior round.
State, behavior and change are deeper than Runtime-specific entities; Operation is not a universal ontology root.
Operation survives as the correct root Runtime commitment entity.
Proposal, Operation, Attempt/Realization, Authority, Resource/Dependency, Effect, Observation/Evidence, Claim/Projection and Reconciliation form the minimal Runtime-specific ontology.
Goal and Semantic Outcome remain adjacent but outside generic Runtime authority.
Process, systemd unit/cgroup and Windows Job Object are realization substrates rather than ontological roots.
RuntimeJobRecord is a current durable Operation record/handle rather than the foundational Operation ontology.
Workspace and Git are current source/resource-context abstractions rather than universal foundations.
SQLite is the current Registry transaction owner rather than a foundational requirement.
Current authority profile names and mechanisms are contingent implementations of deeper trust, authority and isolation semantics.
One Operation may have zero, one, many, partial or opaque Effects; Operation, Attempt, Effect and Resource identities remain distinct.
Reality, Observation, Evidence and Claim remain distinct across all cross-domain falsifiers.
Authority is a foundational reachable-consequence relation broader than OS credentials.
Reconciliation is foundational because failures and open systems create durable epistemic ambiguity.
semanticCompletionEvaluated=false represents a real foundational boundary even though the field itself is contingent.

All mandatory deterministic, concurrent, authority, namespace, transaction, response-loss, finance, cloud, SMTP, Release/Patch and semantic-goal falsifiers preserve the theory when scopes are explicit.
RF11-RF15 scope laws unify under Scope Conservation: ClaimScope <= ActualSupportScope.
Identity Conservation, Epistemic Separation, Authority Locality, Open-World Non-Closure, Recovery by Truth Convergence and Non-Upgrading Composition are durable cross-round laws.
Current Runtime engineering already embodies many frozen principles; research mostly constrains interpretation and future evolution rather than requiring refactoring.
No engineering work is automatically created by freezing Foundations v1.
Twelve explicit FoundationReopenConditions govern future reopening.
Runtime Foundations v1 is frozen.
notes: RF0-RF16 is closed as the first Runtime Foundations research series. Continue through an engineering consumption phase or a separately scoped Host/Harness Foundations program. Reopen Runtime Foundations only under an explicit FoundationReopenCondition.
